newsitem.title: USA: News Corp. in alliance with EchoStar.
newsitem.headline: News Corp. in alliance with EchoStar.

text.p: Media giant News Corp. Ltd., seeking to strengthen its position in the satellite broadcasting business, Monday announced an alliance with U.S. satellite broadcaster EchoStar Communications Corp.

Under the deal, Rupert Murdoch's News Corp., the owner of the Fox television network, would contribute satellites, cash and other assets of $1 billion from its American Sky Broadcasting (AskyB) unit to the joint venture. In return, News Corp. would hold 50 percent of the equity of EchoStar.
EchoStar, based in Englewood, Colorado, is a worldwide manufacturer and distributor of satellite TV products.

News Corp. said the alliance would enable the company to respond to the growing popularity for subscription television services. News Corp. also controls British Sky Broadcasting, orBSkyB, Britain's leading pay-TV provider, and has a satellite TV joint venture in Japan, JSkyB, that is expected to begin full service next year.
"Jointly we will create a dynamic and promising new competitive force in the subscription marketplace," News Corp. Chairman Ruppert Murdoch said in a statement.
EchoStar plans to spin off some assets to shareholders, including its manufacturing an international businesses.
Longtime News Corp. partner long distance telephone company MCI Communications Corp. would hold 20 percent of News Corp.'s 50 percent interest or 10 percent of EchoStar.
Under terms of the agreement, EchoStar's direct broadcast satellite business will remain in Englewood, Colo. and operate under the name Sky, which is News Corp's brand name around the world.
Charles Ergen will remain chief executive officer of EchoStar and Murdoch will become chairman.

The new Sky service is expected to include 7 satellites, more than 500 channels, retransmission of local TV stations in markets representing more than 75 percent of all U.S. television households and low consumer entry cost.
ASkyB is currently building a multi-million dollar broadcast facility in Gilbert, Ariz. to serve as its broadcast hub.
